newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Weaker CZK boosts Czech June CPI,acceleration seen.
newsitem.headline: Weaker CZK boosts Czech June CPI,acceleration seen.

text.p: Czech inflation rebounded in June, partly because of a weaker currency, and analysts said they saw little hope for a quick return to the earlier downtrend.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) on Tuesday released data showing overall prices jumped 1.2 percent month-on-month in June, forcing the year-on-year rate to 6.8 percent, up from June's record low of 6.3 percent.
The sliding average inflation figure, which uses 1993 as a base, edged down to 7.9 percent from 8.0 percent in May, and was down from 8.6 percent in May 1996.
The inflation data were slightly above market expectations, with a Reuters survey of economists on Monday predicting a 0.9 percent monthly increase.

Analysts said much of the rise in the monthly rate was, as expected, due to a crisis in the crown in May and June, which saw the currency fall to record lows before the central bank was forced to freely float it.
"I think that out of the 1.2 percent increase, about one-third is due to the depreciation of the crown," Martin Kupka, an economist at Patria Finance told Reuters.
"And I think we can expect relatively high inflation in July...There will still be some effect on prices next month, but it will be much less," he added.
The Czech crown came under a heavy downward pressure at the end of May as speculators targeted the currency as overvalued, and the ruling coalition government teetered near a possible collapse.
The central bank was eventually forced on May 27 to float the currency and abandon its 15 percent fluctuation band within which it would fix the currency against a mark/dollar peg.

The CSU said that the largest influence on inflation in June were prices of foodstuffs, tobacco and beverages, which rose 2.0 percent, month-on-month, accounting for some 53 percent of the overall rise.
Household goods and leisure prices, heavily influenced by the weakening of the crown, also recorded above average increases in June.
Martin Hlusek of Expanida Finance said he expects inflation for the year to be between 8.5-9 percent.
"This applies only in the case that there is no radical pressure on wage growth, or a large deviation in the crown rate," he said.
The crown itself was steady on Tuesday with dealers saying the market had already built in the expected-high June figure.
The central bank fixed the crown at 32.474 to the dollar and 18.496 to the mark, little changed from the market opening.
Analysts also said July inflation will jump substantially due to a loosening of rents and energy prices by an average of 50 percent and 15 percent respectively, effective July 1.
Many Czechs still live in flats with artificially low rents and with energy bills subsidised by industrial users.
